memory_candidates.content: lake-build-guard.sh build mode requires a lake SUBCOMMAND as the first lake argument: `-- build FormalSystem`, never `-- FormalSystem` (exit 77, nothing built). Piping the guard through `tail`/`grep` reports the pipeline's exit status, so a build that never ran reads as exit 0. Always capture the guard's own status: `set -o pipefail` with `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, or redirect to a file and append `echo GUARD_EXIT=$?`.

`lake env lean <file>` does NOT apply the lakefile's Mathlib linter options: a file can elaborate with exit 0 and no output yet raise linter warnings (e.g. the `show` tactic linter, which wants `change` when the goal is actually changed) in the real lake build. Single-file elaboration is a fast proof check only; only the guarded lake build is authoritative for a warning-free gate.

When a shared file carries another session's uncommitted hunks, git-commit-scoped.sh cannot commit only your hunks (it commits whole paths from the working tree). Leave the file unstaged, say so in the commit message and handoff, and mark the phase [PARTIAL]: [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] is inadmissible because its condition 5 (no residual work) fails. Before staging any shared doc, diff it and confirm every hunk is yours.
